content.comment_body: Hello, In [product_name] [version_no], when using UDF blocks with flags (for example, 10 instances of UDF B containing 2 nested instances of UDF A, each with 1 flag), you might encounter unexpected use of special flags such as M30 and M31, even though regular flags are still available. To address this issue: 1) Explicitly declare all special flags in your program; 2) Insert the required UDFs; 3) Remove any unused special flags.

analysis.insight_summary: Users working with complex nested UDFs in [product_name] [version_no] notice that the software automatically assigns special flags (like M30 and M31) even when regular flags could be used instead. This behavior occurs during workflows involving multiple nested UDF instances and may complicate debugging or maintenance, due to unintended allocation of reserved memory locations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to prioritize the allocation of available regular flags for UDF instances and only use special flags when necessary. They also want predictable and manageable flag assignment within their programs.
